question: What primary hormone is responsible for softening ligaments during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin is produced by the placenta and corpus luteum to loosen ligaments and prepare the pelvis for birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why do pregnant women often experience an increase in shoe size?

options.A: Calcium moves from the foot bones to nourish the growing fetus
options.B: Hormones cause foot ligaments and arches to relax and flatten
options.C: Fluid retention in the toes makes feet permanently longer
options.D: Extra body weight permanently breaks the bones in the feet

explanation: Circulating hormones loosen connective tissue in the feet, leading to a permanent flattening of the arches. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: The abnormal forward shift of the maternal center of gravity causes what spinal curvature?
explanation: Lordosis is the excessive inward curvature of the lower back that develops to balance the growing belly. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: A pregnant woman stands leaning backward. What mechanical problem is her body trying to solve?

options.A: Shifting the heavy uterus backward to align with the center of gravity
options.B: Reducing severe muscle spasms in the upper thoracic region
options.C: Accommodating the widening of the pelvic outlet for delivery
options.D: Relieving pressure from the compressed diaphragm and lungs

explanation: The body leans back to counteract the forward pull of the heavy pregnancy weight. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: What term describes the painful inflammation and excessive movement of the front pubic joint?
explanation: Symphysis pubis dysfunction occurs when the pelvic joints become too loose and painful during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: A pregnant patient complains of sharp pain when turning over in bed and getting out of a car. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Severe calcium deficiency in the long bones
options.B: Herniated lumbar disc pressing on the sciatic nerve
options.C: Excessive movement at the pubic symphysis joint
options.D: Early onset of rheumatoid arthritis in the hips

explanation: Asymmetrical leg movements stretch the unstable pubic symphysis, triggering sharp pain in women with pelvic girdle relaxation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary reason pregnant women develop a characteristic waddling gait?

options.A: Joint laxity and a shifted center of gravity
options.B: Weakening of the quadriceps muscle group
options.C: Severe cartilage loss inside the knee joints
options.D: Permanent shortening of the Achilles tendon

explanation: Loose pelvic joints combined with a forward shift in weight force women to widen their stance and waddle when walking. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience painful calf cramps during the third trimester?

options.A: Rapid buildup of lactic acid from excessive daily exercise
options.B: Total depletion of iron stores in the lower leg muscles
options.C: Venous stasis and circulatory changes in the lower limbs
options.D: Complete blockage of arterial blood flow to the feet

explanation: Poor venous return and pressure from the uterus create sluggish blood flow, which triggers painful muscle spasms. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: What happens to the pelvic joints during the descent of the fetus in labour?

options.A: They lock tightly together to protect the spinal cord
options.B: They undergo further passive stretching to widen the pelvis
options.C: They begin immediate bone fusion and calcification
options.D: They shrink in size to push the baby out faster

explanation: The movable joints of the pelvis stretch passively to maximize the space available for the baby to pass through. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why is careful patient positioning important during labour when regional anesthesia is used?

options.A: The mother will lose all voluntary control of her arm muscles
options.B: Anesthesia causes the bones to become completely brittle and fragile
options.C: The patient cannot feel pain warning signs if joints are overstretched
options.D: Poor positioning stops the baby from moving down the birth canal

explanation: Regional anesthesia numbs pain signals, meaning the woman will not feel if her joints or muscles are placed in a harmful position. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the term for the separation of the abdominal wall muscles during pregnancy?
explanation: Diastasis recti is the parting of the rectus abdominis muscles as the belly expands to house the growing baby. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: Why do some women experience chronic back pain long after giving birth?

options.A: Slow recovery of joint stability combined with repeated heavy lifting
options.B: Complete destruction of the lumbar vertebrae during labour
options.C: Rapid loss of bone density from drinking too much milk
options.D: Permanent shortening of the spine caused by epidural anesthesia

explanation: Loose joints take months to tighten up, and bending over a baby strains an already vulnerable back. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: Numbness and tingling in the fingers during pregnancy are classic signs of what condition?
explanation: Fluid retention in the wrist compresses the median nerve, causing tingling and numbness in the hand. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)

question: A pregnant woman complains of severe lower back pain and an unstable pelvis. What nursing advice is most appropriate?

options.A: Take high-dose calcium tablets and complete strict bed rest
options.B: Apply ice packs directly to the lower spine for six hours daily
options.C: Avoid walking entirely until after the baby is safely delivered
options.D: Wear a supportive pelvic belt and practice safe body mechanics

explanation: Support belts help stabilize loose pelvic joints, and proper body mechanics protect the spine from further strain. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)
